Telescope 5.0 is, once again, the biggest update yet (I know, I keep saying that, but this time the whole desktop app got rewritten in Rust). It starts about three times faster and uses less CPU while streaming. The phone app and the protocol didn't change, and your phones work without pairing again.

## Faster

Measured on my 8 core Linux machine, streaming 1080p at 30 fps with all the default plugins on.

- Opens in 0.3 s instead of 0.9 s.
- CPU while streaming went from 23% of one core to 17%, and with hardware decoding from 18% to 7%.
- Takes about 68 MB on disk instead of about 664 MB.
- Over USB on Linux, every frame arrives up to 40 ms sooner.

Memory use is about the same as before. I haven't measured Windows yet.

## Things to know

- **Plugins written in Python don't run any more.** They have to be rewritten in Lua (shaders in WGSL, cards in `.slint`). `docs/writing-plugins.md` has the details, and `check-plugin` checks one from the terminal and points at the line of a shader error.
- **Linux no longer needs Python.** It only needs v4l2loopback and adb is optional. The VA-API setup button is gone because hardware decoding now finds the graphics card by itself (VA-API or CUDA on Linux, Direct3D 11 on Windows) and the line under the switch shows which one it's using.
- **The first start cleans up after Python**, removing the old `lib-` folders and the leftover requirements files.
- **You can go back to the Python version (4.4.2, its last release)** in Settings, Updates, **Go back to the Python version**. It saves a dated copy of your settings first, keeps your paired phones and turns off 4.4.2's own update check to stop it from offering the Rust version again. Settings and Lua plugins added since then don't carry over. The phone app has to match: uninstall the newer one first, since Android won't downgrade it, then install the 4.4.2 apk and pair again.
- On Linux going back sets up Python's libraries first, which needs the internet, Python 3.12 or newer with venv, and a few minutes. If that fails nothing is changed. An AppImage can't swap itself and opens the 4.4.2 download page instead. I haven't tried going back on a real Windows PC.

## New

- AppImage (`Telescope-x86_64.AppImage`) for Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer. It doesn't need libfuse2.
- Every colour grading control can go on a keyboard shortcut and there is an **Add phone shortcut**.
- **Reset to defaults** on the Plugins tab replaces Turn all back on. Optional plugins go off and the rest go on.
- Plugins can read the person mask in their shaders.

## Fixed

- Browser camera in Firefox now holds the resolution you picked at about the frame rate you asked for. Before, Firefox dropped to 2 fps and kept streaming at that for the rest of the call.
- VHS, CRT, Desk mode and Background blur ran at 16 to 20 fps on a real stream. They hold the full frame rate at 1080p now.
- Full-range JPEG greys were crushed (16 and 235 turned into pure black and white).
- Saved virtual camera slots work again and a browser's settings are only saved once you change something.
- Downloads retry after a timeout instead of failing.
- A failed update on Windows rolls back everything it changed.
- Settings and plugin windows stay above the main window and Wayland windows get their icon.
- The Windows exe has its icon and name, which the tray and the firewall prompt show.
